title.en: The poet and the call to count to twelve

heading.en: What if the whole world paused?

hook.en: Imagine every engine, every voice and every argument on Earth stopping together for a few seconds. Pablo Neruda asks us to imagine exactly that in Keeping Quiet.

objectives.en: Introduce Pablo Neruda and the background of the poem
Explain the poet's request to count to twelve and keep still
Interpret the significance of the number twelve

narration.en: Imagine every engine, every voice and every argument on Earth stopping together for a few seconds. Pablo Neruda asks us to imagine exactly that in Keeping Quiet.

body.en: Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet and diplomat who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971. Keeping Quiet was written in Spanish and is studied in an English translation. In it the poet asks all of humanity to count to twelve and then stay still and silent together for a short while.

points.en: Written in Spanish; read in translation
Request: count to twelve, then be still and silent

narration.en: Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet and diplomat who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971. Keeping Quiet was written in Spanish and is studied in an English translation. In it the poet asks all of humanity to count to twelve and then stay still and silent together for a short while.
Let us see why the poet chooses the number twelve.

say.en: In the centre we write the poet's request.
Twelve is the number of hours on a clock face.

text.en: on the face of a clock

say.en: There are twelve signs of the zodiac.
So twelve suggests time and a complete cycle.
The pause is short: only as long as counting to twelve.
In silence we need no language, so no one is divided.

body.en: The poet wants everyone to stop speaking in any language and to stop moving their arms so much, just for a second. Without words and without rush, all people would be equal and together. He calls this an exotic, or rare and strange, moment.

points.en: Stop moving: no rush, no engines
All people together in one rare moment

narration.en: The poet wants everyone to stop speaking in any language and to stop moving their arms so much, just for a second. Without words and without rush, all people would be equal and together. He calls this an exotic, or rare and strange, moment.

body.en: Remember why twelve matters with three Cs: the Clock has twelve hours, the Calendar has twelve months, and the Cosmos has twelve zodiac signs.

narration.en: Remember why twelve matters with three Cs: the Clock has twelve hours, the Calendar has twelve months, and the Cosmos has twelve zodiac signs.

problem.en: Why does the poet ask us to count to twelve?

steps.en: Explain twelve as a symbol of time: hours, months, zodiac signs.
Show the purpose: a short, shared pause for all humanity.
Link to the poem: stillness to reflect on ourselves.

answer.en: Twelve suggests time: twelve hours on a clock, twelve months and twelve zodiac signs. The poet asks us to count to twelve so that all humanity pauses together for a short time, to be still, silent and reflect.
